from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Linear equations define constraints in our spatial world.",
            "Imagine a robot arm constrained by these equations.",
            "The intersection of these constraints identifies a pose."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems", lecture_lines)
        
        # Axis and setup
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        self.add(axes)
        
        v1 = Vector([2, 1], color="#FF5733")
        v2 = Vector([1, 2], color="#FF5733")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            ORIGIN, v1.get_end(), v1.get_end() + v2.get_end(), v2.get_end(),
            fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#33FF57", stroke_width=0
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(parallelogram))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF33")
        equation = MathTex(r"c_1v_1 + c_2v_2 = b").set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        
        # Add b vector
        b = Vector([3, 3], color="#33FFFF")
        self.play(Create(b))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrices act as transformations on a grid.",
            "The inverse matrix functions as an undo button.",
            "Singular matrices flatten space, losing original information."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Inverse Matrix: Unpacking the Transformation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        matrix_a = MathTex("A").set_color("#FF5733")
        inverse_a = MathTex("A^{-1}").set_color("#33FF57")
        identity = MathTex("I").set_color("#FFFF33")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_at_grid(inverse_a, "B5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(inverse_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF33"))
        self.place_at_grid(identity, "D4", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(identity))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Column Space: The 'Reachable' World", [
            "Column space represents all reachable transformation outputs.",
            "Visualize this as a span of vector columns.",
            "The cat's reachable movement defines its column space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show column vectors as directions in space.
        col_v1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FF5733")
        col_v2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.2, color="#FF5733")
        cols = VGroup(col_v1, col_v2)
        self.place_at_grid(cols, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(cols))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize the span of columns as a 2D plane.
        plane = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2, RIGHT*2 + UP*1.5, UP*1.5, 
                        fill_color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_color="#33FF57")
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Indicate a vector b that lies within the plane.
        vec_b = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.2 + UP*0.8, color="#FFFF33")
        self.place_at_grid(vec_b, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_b))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Null space contains vectors mapped to the origin.",
            "These are directions squashed into zero space.",
            "Think of the security camera's hidden line."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Null Space: The 'Hidden' Kernel", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        plane = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        vector_v = Vector([1, 1], color="#FF5733")
        origin_dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        kernel_label = Text("Kernel", color="#33FF57", font_size=20)
        null_space_line = Line(start=[-2, -2, 0], end=[2, 2, 0], color="#FFFF33", stroke_width=4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(origin_dot, "B2")
        self.play(Create(plane), GrowFromCenter(origin_dot))
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_v.move_to(self.grid["B2"] + np.array([-0.5, -0.5, 0]))))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(kernel_label, "C4")
        self.play(FadeIn(kernel_label))
        self.play(vector_v.animate.move_to(self.grid["B2"]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.place_at_grid(null_space_line, "B2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(null_space_line))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesizing the Big Picture", [
            "Invertibility requires a non-empty, unique space solution.",
            "Null space collapsing points prevents perfect reconstruction.",
            "Mapping these spaces defines our full system picture."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        # Subspaces
        col_space = Ellipse(width=2, height=1.5, color="#FF5733").set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        null_space = Circle(radius=0.7, color="#33FF57").set_fill(opacity=0.3)
        rank_nullity_eq = MathTex(r"dim(Col) + dim(Null) = n", font_size=36, color="#FFFF33")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.place_in_area(col_space, "A2", "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(col_space), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.place_at_grid(null_space, "D5")
        self.play(FadeIn(null_space), run_time=1)
        
        # Orthogonal lines
        ortho_line = Line(col_space.get_center(), null_space.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(ortho_line), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.place_at_grid(rank_nullity_eq, "F3")
        self.play(Write(rank_nullity_eq), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Geometric Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Systems to Spaces

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
sections.content: Introduce Ax=b as the intersection of hyperplanes. Visualize the system as constraints in space. Prerequisite: Basic understanding of vectors as coordinate points.
sections.example: A robot arm with two joints: each linear equation represents a constraint on an angle; their intersection is the specific pose of the arm.

sections.title: The Inverse Matrix: Unpacking the Transformation
sections.content: View the matrix A as a transformation grid. The inverse A⁻¹ is the 'undo' button. Explain that if a system is flattened (determinant 0), it cannot be undone.
sections.example: A photo-editing tool: Matrix A scales and rotates an image; A⁻¹ acts as the 'Reset' button that returns pixels to their original coordinates.

sections.title: Column Space: The 'Reachable' World
sections.content: Define Column Space as the span of the columns of A. Visually, it is the set of all possible output vectors b that the transformation can 'land on'.
sections.example: A cat moving in a 2D room: If the cat can only move along a specific diagonal plank, the column space is just that 1D line, regardless of how large the room is.

sections.title: Null Space: The 'Hidden' Kernel
sections.content: Define Null Space as the set of vectors x where Ax = 0. Visually, these are the directions that get 'squashed' into the origin.
sections.example: A security camera projection: Any movement of a person along the line of sight of the lens results in no change in the image (the projection is 0); that line of sight is the Null Space.

sections.title: Synthesizing the Big Picture
sections.content: Connect the concepts: If the Null Space contains only the zero vector, the transformation is invertible, and every point is reachable.
sections.example: A 3D printer: The 'Column Space' is the printable volume; the 'Null Space' represents design flaws where multiple distinct parts compress into the same coordinate, causing print failure.
